{{short description|Central American seafood soup}}
'''Tapado''' is a seafood soup served in [[Central America]]n countries such as [[Guatemala]] and [[Honduras]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://hispanickitchen.com/recipes/tapado-costeno-honduran-seafood-coconut-milk-soup/|title=Tapado Costeño: Honduran Seafood and Coconut Milk Soup|work=Hispanic Kitchen|access-date=2018-10-24|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-10-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024073657/https://hispanickitchen.com/recipes/tapado-costeno-honduran-seafood-coconut-milk-soup/|url-status=dead}}</ref> It uses coconut milk and seafood as well as plantains. Within these countries, tapado is associated with the [[Garifuna]] community.<ref name="Revue Magazine">{{cite web |last1=Rose |first1=Natalie |title=Coconut milk and boat-fresh seafood creates a Río Dulce specialty and the garífuna's most beloved dish |url=http://www.revuemag.com/2012/11/tapado/ |website=Revue Magazine |publisher=Revue Magazine |access-date=24 October 2018 |date=2012-11-03 |archive-date=2018-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181024073653/http://www.revuemag.com/2012/11/tapado/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
